requirements_summary: Primary: Dedicated capacity to run workforce-facing chat assistant (bridge crew + ops) with strict latency SLOs and predictable monthly cost. Secondary: reranking for document retrieval pipelines. Must support VPC private control plane, KMS key management, audit logs, and EU data residency for some customers.
workload_profile: Mixed: interactive chat is latency-sensitive (short-turns 60-300 tokens); batch reranking and document embedding pipelines are throughput-heavy but elastic. Peak traffic windows: daily 10:00-12:00 and 18:00-19:30 UTC with bursts tied to fleet events.
sizing_assumptions: Steady-state baseline: 8 QPS. Typical request: 60 input tokens + 180 output tokens = 240 tokens/request. Observed 95th percentile burst: 42 QPS sustained for ~6 minutes during events. Target P95 latency: <= 300ms for common short responses; 95th for long generation <= 800ms.
raw_capacity_calcs: Baseline tokens/sec steady-state: 8 QPS * 240 tokens = 1920 tokens/sec
Burst tokens/sec (observed peak): 42 QPS * 240 tokens = 10080 tokens/sec
Desired headroom: 1.5x for sudden spikes => planning peak cap ~15k tokens/sec
Per-H100 sustainable tokens/sec (avg, inference profile): ~2500-3200 tokens/sec depending on quantization and batching
Recommended initial reserved footprint: 5 x H100 (active) + 1 x H100 warm standby = ~15k-18k tokens/sec peak capacity with autoscale to additional on-demand units
Fallback plan: lightweight CPU-backed reranker for non-latency-critical traffic to reduce GPU load during sustained events
latency_and_slos: Requested: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 300ms for 1-turn short replies (<=150 tokens). For multi-turn long replies (>=250 tokens) p95 <= 800ms. Redwood to provide measurable per-route SLO dashboards and token-level cost breakdown per route.
throughput_guarantees_and_sla_items: Require committed baseline throughput 10k tokens/sec during business hours with credits for overage and defined remediation steps for sustained under-provision. SLA negotiation points: MTTR for capacity degradations, notice windows for maintenance, and automated fallback routing to a cheaper variant if Dedicated pool saturated.
procurement_notes: Procurement wants 12-month term with quarterly usage review. Legal asks: indemnity clarifications and data residency addendum. Finance prefers flat committed monthly invoice vs pay-as-you-go spikes.
workshop_outputs: Sizing worksheet v1 (attached) with per-route QPS & tokens/sec breakdown
Recommended infra: 5 H100 active + 1 warm standby; option to add 3 A100 cost-tier nodes for burst offload
Runbook: automated scale-up triggers (burst QPS > 30 for >2 mins), degraded-mode routing to reranker
SLA draft: baseline throughput, latency SLOs, remediation commitments
poe_and_technical_decisions: Model family: will use a verified open model family with Redwood-tested kernels. Preference for H100 for latency-sensitive routes; consider quantized variants for batch reranking. KV cache for multi-turn sessions enabled to reduce per-token compute during long dialogues.
cost_sensitivity: Medium-high: willing to commit to reserved capacity in exchange for price predictability and latency guarantees. Finance requires 2 pricing scenarios: 6-month and 12-month commit.
